---
title: "New Accounts and Idle Account Rate"
description: "Accounts created per day, and the share that never reached a partner service."
---

New CanadaLogin accounts per day, and how many of them never used a partner
service. A jump in the idle rate is a sign of bot sign-ups.

This is the one IBM Verify metric that reads the [raw event
stream](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw.qmd), because no summary table
records when an account first appears.

## Calculation

An account is **new** on the ET day of its first event in
[`authentication_activity`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/authentication_activity.qmd).
It is **idle** if it has no successful event in
[`application_usage`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/application_usage.qmd)
for a public application. Public means not flagged internal in
[`rp.service`](../../catalog/rp/service.qmd); an application with no row in
[`rp.alias`](../../catalog/rp/alias.qmd) counts as public, because internal
applications are the ones registered on purpose and a new partner can go live
before it is added.

There are three idle windows:

- **Ever:** no public use at all yet. Keeps falling as accounts age.
- **14 days:** no public use within 14 days of the first event. Final once 14
  days have passed.
- **Same day:** no public use by the end of the ET day the account was made.
  Final the next morning, so it is the one to use for spotting bot days.

Leave out a blank user ID. The user ID `"UNKNOWN"` counts as one account, as it
does in the summary tables (see [notes](../notes.qmd)).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

By day:

```sql
WITH first_seen AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        min(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.authentication_activity
    WHERE subject <> ''
    GROUP BY subject
),
new_accounts AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        first_ts,
        -- time is a UTC string; report on ET days
        date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') AS created_on
    FROM first_seen
),
public_use AS (
    SELECT
        userid,
        min(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_public_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.application_usage
    WHERE result = 'success'
      -- only internal applications are left out; an unmapped one is public
      AND applicationname NOT IN (
          SELECT al.alias
          FROM rp.alias al
          JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
          WHERE s.is_internal
      )
    GROUP BY userid
)

SELECT
    n.created_on,
    count(*) AS new_accounts,
    count_if(p.userid IS NULL) AS idle_accounts,
    count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR p.first_public_ts > n.first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY) AS idle_accounts_14d,
    count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR date(with_timezone(p.first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') > n.created_on) AS idle_accounts_same_day,
    CAST(count_if(p.userid IS NULL) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS idle_rate,
    CAST(count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR p.first_public_ts > n.first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS idle_rate_14d,
    CAST(count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR date(with_timezone(p.first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') > n.created_on) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS idle_rate_same_day
FROM new_accounts n
LEFT JOIN public_use p ON n.subject = p.userid
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE n.created_on BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY n.created_on
ORDER BY n.created_on;
```

Since launch, point in time:

```sql
WITH first_seen AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        min(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.authentication_activity
    WHERE subject <> ''
    GROUP BY subject
),
new_accounts AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') AS created_on
    FROM first_seen
),
public_use AS (
    SELECT
        userid,
        min(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_public_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.application_usage
    WHERE result = 'success'
      AND applicationname NOT IN (
          SELECT al.alias
          FROM rp.alias al
          JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
          WHERE s.is_internal
      )
    GROUP BY userid
),
-- accounts made each day, and accounts that first used a public service each day
daily AS (
    SELECT created_on AS day, count(*) AS created, 0 AS activated
    FROM new_accounts
    GROUP BY created_on
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        date(with_timezone(p.first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') AS day,
        0 AS created,
        count(*) AS activated
    FROM new_accounts n
    JOIN public_use p ON n.subject = p.userid
    GROUP BY date(with_timezone(p.first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')
)

SELECT
    day,
    sum(sum(created)) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS accounts,
    sum(sum(created) - sum(activated)) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS idle_accounts
FROM daily
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```

## R

By day:

```r
first_seen <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "authentication_activity")) |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), subject != "") |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(subject) |>
  summarise(first_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  # time is a UTC string; report on ET days
  mutate(created_on = sql("date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')"))

# only internal applications are left out; an unmapped one is public
internal_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(is_internal) |>
  select(applicationname = alias)

public_use <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "application_usage")) |>
  filter(result == "success") |>
  anti_join(internal_apps, by = "applicationname") |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  summarise(first_public_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(first_public_day = sql("date(with_timezone(first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')"))

first_seen |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    created_on >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    created_on <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  left_join(public_use, by = c("subject" = "userid")) |>
  mutate(
    idle = is.na(first_public_ts),
    idle_14d = is.na(first_public_ts) | first_public_ts > sql("first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY"),
    idle_same_day = is.na(first_public_ts) | first_public_day > created_on
  ) |>
  group_by(created_on) |>
  summarise(
    new_accounts = n(),
    idle_accounts = sum(as.integer(idle), na.rm = TRUE),
    idle_accounts_14d = sum(as.integer(idle_14d), na.rm = TRUE),
    idle_accounts_same_day = sum(as.integer(idle_same_day), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    idle_rate = as.numeric(idle_accounts) / new_accounts,
    idle_rate_14d = as.numeric(idle_accounts_14d) / new_accounts,
    idle_rate_same_day = as.numeric(idle_accounts_same_day) / new_accounts
  ) |>
  arrange(created_on)
```

Since launch, point in time:

```r
first_seen <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "authentication_activity")) |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), subject != "") |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(subject) |>
  summarise(first_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(created_on = sql("date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')"))

internal_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(is_internal) |>
  select(applicationname = alias)

public_use <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "application_usage")) |>
  filter(result == "success") |>
  anti_join(internal_apps, by = "applicationname") |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  summarise(first_public_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(first_public_day = sql("date(with_timezone(first_public_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')"))

# accounts made each day, and accounts that first used a public service each day
created <- first_seen |>
  count(day = created_on, name = "created") |>
  mutate(activated = 0L)

activated <- first_seen |>
  inner_join(public_use, by = c("subject" = "userid")) |>
  count(day = first_public_day, name = "activated") |>
  mutate(created = 0L)

union_all(created, activated) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(
    created = sum(created, na.rm = TRUE),
    activated = sum(activated, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  window_order(day) |>
  mutate(
    accounts = cumsum(created),
    idle_accounts = cumsum(created - activated)
  ) |>
  select(day, accounts, idle_accounts) |>
  arrange(day)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Idle accounts are a signal, not a bot count.** Some real people sign up and
never use a service. Normal days run about 10% to 15% idle. On bot-wave days,
nearly all new accounts are idle.

**Pick the window for the question.** To spot a bot day, use the same-day rate:
it is final the next morning. To compare months, use the 14-day rate: the "ever"
rate keeps falling as accounts have more time to reach a service, so recent days
look worse than old ones, and the last 14 days of any window are still
provisional on the 14-day rate.

**New accounts add up across days, rates do not.** Each account has one creation
day, so summing `new_accounts` or `idle_accounts` over days is correct. Recompute
a rate over a longer window from the summed counts.

**Since launch is point in time.** An account leaves the idle count on the day it
first uses a public service, and earlier days are never restated. So the idle
count on a past day is what it was on that day, not how many of those accounts
are still idle now. The other choice, restating history, would shrink every past
day's idle count as accounts later reach a service.

**When an account appears.** Most new accounts first appear with a successful
password, which suggests the sign-up flow signs an account in once the password
is set, before any MFA. A few first appear through a token exchange instead,
possibly migrated accounts. Both readings are observed, not confirmed with the
sign-up flow's owners.

**It is expensive.** The query reads both raw tables from launch, and the cost
grows every month. Run it for a reporting window, not on a schedule.

## Alternative names

- new accounts
- sign-ups
- account creations
- registrations
- idle accounts
- dormant accounts
- accounts with no service use
- accounts since launch
- total accounts
